content.title: About
content.content: Black olives are the ripe fruits of the olive tree (Olea europaea) that are typically fermented in brine or a marinade. They have a mild, slightly salty flavor, a meaty texture, and a characteristic dark purple‑black color.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Black olives are produced from green olives by additional fermentation, not by natural ripening.
The olive tree has been a symbol of peace and victory in ancient Greece and Rome.
Olive oil, extracted from olives, is a cornerstone of the Mediterranean diet.
In ancient Rome olives were used as a form of payment and as diplomatic gifts.
Black olives are commonly served as a snack alongside wine and cheese platters.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Black olives contain polyphenols such as oleuropein that help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Monounsaturated fats in olive oil help lower LDL‑cholesterol levels.

items.title: Contains vitamin E
items.content: Vitamin E acts as an antioxidant, protecting cell membranes and supporting immune function.

items.title: Source of iron and copper
items.content: These minerals are involved in hemoglobin formation and energy metabolism.

items.title: Aids digestion
items.content: The fiber in olives promotes regular bowel movements.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Because black olives are often cured in brine, excessive consumption can raise blood pressure.

items.title: Olive allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to olives or olive oil.

items.title: Oleuropein sensitivity
items.content: In large amounts, oleuropein can cause gastrointestinal discomfort.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Black olives can be enjoyed as a snack, added to salads, pastas, pizza, tapas, or used in sauces and marinades. They are often served in oil with herbs or in a wine‑vinegar brine.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep olives in their original brine in a sealed jar in the refrigerator. Properly stored, they last several months. Discard any olives that develop mold, off‑odors, or an off‑taste.
